name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification. The dataset covers European cities distributed in over 34 countries and includes classes such as annual crop, permanent crop, pasture, highway, residential buildings, industrial buildings, river, sea & lake, forest, and herbaceous vegetation.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
publisher: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence (DFKI) / TU Kaiserslautern
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2 [cs.CV], 2019.
rai:dataCollection: Satellite images were downloaded from the Sentinel-2A satellite via Amazon S3. Images were selected from European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas, distributed over 34 European countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected. Images were recorded throughout the year to capture high variance in land use and land cover classes. 64x64 pixel image patches were extracted and manually checked multiple times to correct ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images and images full of snow or ice.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Images with clouds, mislabeling, dead pixels, or ice/snow were identified and discarded during manual checking. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast; extreme cases were retained in the dataset to advocate the classifier to learn these cases.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite images provided by the Sentinel-2A satellite, downloaded via Amazon S3. The satellite images are openly and freely accessible through ESA's Copernicus Earth observation program. Land use and land cover class information was derived from the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Images were extracted from recordings spanning at least from December 2015 to March 2017, covering all seasons throughout the year.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Bands with a lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. For comparative evaluation, RGB images were computed by combining the red (B04), green (B03), and blue (B02) bands. Multiple Sentinel-2 images were merged, adjacent polygons of the same class were dissolved, and all bands were resampled to 10m resolution before cropping 64x64 image patches.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images with low cloud levels were selected. Multiple Sentinel-2 images were merged. Classes from the European Urban Atlas were merged into 10 considered classes. Adjacent polygons of the same class were dissolved. All bands were resampled to 10m resolution. 64x64 pixel image patches were cropped. Mislabeled or broken image patches (e.g., those containing clouds, dead pixels, snow, or ice) were filtered out through multiple rounds of manual checking.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels were derived from the European Urban Atlas land use and land cover mapping. All 27,000 images were manually checked multiple times by the authors to correct the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The 10 classes were chosen based on the principle that they are visible at 10 meters per pixel resolution and are frequently enough covered by the European Urban Atlas to generate thousands of image patches.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were discarded. Images with atmospheric effects causing color casts were retained intentionally to allow the classifier to learn these cases.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables real-world Earth observation applications including land use and land cover change detection (e.g., detecting deforestation, urban development, demolition of industrial buildings), and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date (e.g., OpenStreetMap). Applications are relevant for agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change monitoring, urban development, and environmental monitoring. Deforestation detection is highlighted as particularly important for climate change mitigation and identifying illegal forest clearing.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of cities represented per country in the European Urban Atlas, leading to uneven geographic coverage across European countries. The dataset is limited to Europe. Networks pretrained on ILSVRC-2012 were initially not trained on images other than RGB images, which may affect performance on non-RGB band combinations.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is based on Sentinel-2 satellite images with a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel, which does not allow fine-grained per-pixel segmentation. The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The dataset is limited to 10 land use and land cover classes visible at 10m resolution. Coverage is limited to European cities included in the European Urban Atlas.
rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of machine learning models for land use and land cover classification. The dataset is intended for benchmarking deep learning approaches (CNNs) for satellite image classification. Applications include land use and land cover change detection, improvement and verification of geographical maps (e.g., OpenStreetMap), environmental monitoring, urban development monitoring, and deforestation detection.
